recent_posts.title: How to render interactive HTML inside a canvas element with shader effects
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of an experimental browser feature that allows rendering real, interactive HTML inside a Canvas element, enabling shader and visual effects like water simulations to be applied directly to live UI. The feature requires enabling a Chrome flag and is not yet production-ready. Several community demos are showcased, including ice effects, page-peel transitions, and glow animations. The author built their own water-effect demo using Claude Code over roughly 15 iterative prompts, and recommends adding fine-tune control panels to streamline the AI-assisted iteration process.

OpenAI Image 2.0 vs Gemini models tested in a real landscaping app
recent_posts.summary: A practical comparison of OpenAI Image 2.0 against Google's Gemini models (referred to as 'Nano Banana Pro' and Flash) across eight real-world landscaping visualization tasks. Tests include adding plants, removing trees, inserting fire pits, pergolas, water features, and swimming pools into photos of actual homes. OpenAI Image 2.0 generally produces more photorealistic results and better adheres to reference image assets, but is significantly slower and more expensive. Gemini Flash is faster and cheaper but less realistic, while Gemini Pro falls in between. The author plans to offer both a fast/cheap (Flash) and slow/quality (Image 2.0) option in their landscaping SaaS app.

recent_posts.title: Building a landing page with Claude Design step by step
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on demo of Claude Design (claude.ai/design) used to build a landing page for a landscaping AI service. The creator walks through the iterative prompting process, showing interactive before/after sections, Three.js shader effects, orbiting plant animations, parallax scrolling, and floating leaf graphics. Key takeaway: Claude Design is not a one-shot tool — it requires multiple rounds of prompting, design sensibility, and frontend knowledge to produce polished results. The workflow involves setting up a design system from an existing codebase, then iterating on sections, and finally handing off to Claude Code for integration.

recent_posts.title: NEW Claude Feature - Setting up your First Routine
recent_posts.summary: Claude has introduced a new feature called Routines — scheduled, AI-powered tasks similar to cron jobs but with built-in intelligence and decision-making. Using Claude Code CLI, you can set up routines via claude.ai/code with a name, a system prompt, a schedule, and environment variables. A practical walkthrough demonstrates building a 4-hour email notifier that filters sponsorship emails via Zoho Mail and sends SMS alerts via Twilio. Key distinction: use routines when the task requires AI judgment; use traditional cron jobs for simple, deterministic automation. Routines run on your Claude subscription rather than API billing, making them more cost-effective for recurring tasks.

recent_posts.title: How AI tools changed my UI/UX design workflow
recent_posts.summary: A UI/UX designer shares how their workflow has shifted with AI tools. Instead of starting in Figma from scratch, they now use Claude Code for initial vibe-design prototyping, then use Figma MCP to generate multiple design variations quickly. The designer picks the best option, refines colors and layout manually in Figma, then feeds the result back to Claude Code to implement in live code. The workflow produced a working floating modal panel with filtering and search in minutes, without writing any code directly. The author positions AI as a junior designer that handles iteration while the human designer handles refinement and creative judgment.

recent_posts.title: Using Remotion to generate dynamic videos from web tech in a real app
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of using Remotion to generate dynamic MP4 videos from web technologies (HTML/CSS) within a landscaping AI app. The demo shows how a Figma design is converted into animated video slides via an AI coding agent (Claude Code CLI) with Figma MCP integration, pulling asset data from a database to produce a proposal video for landscaping clients. The result is a dynamic, data-driven video pipeline where each plant or hardscaping asset gets its own animated slide.

recent_posts.title: Claude Mythos and OpenAI hype are marketing not breakthroughs
recent_posts.summary: A skeptical take on the hype surrounding Anthropic's Claude Mythos and OpenAI's upcoming cybersecurity-focused model, both released only to select companies. The author argues that limited releases are primarily a marketing tactic used to generate hype and raise capital, not evidence of genuinely dangerous capabilities. Drawing on personal experience building with AI tools, the author cautions against 'AI psychosis' — the tendency to get swept up in excitement before actually using a model — and urges a wait-and-see approach grounded in real usage rather than influencer reactions.

recent_posts.title: Building an AI landscaping SaaS app with Claude Code
recent_posts.summary: A developer showcases an AI-powered landscaping SaaS app built using Claude Code, demonstrating features like image-based landscaping visualization, iterative AI-generated design changes (adding pools, vines, seasonal effects), an asset library of 500+ vegetation elements generated with Google Image Gen 4, and a video orbit feature. The app uses a Figma-like open canvas UI designed with help from a Figma MCP server. The creator is building this as part of an early-access course teaching how to use Claude Code to build AI-powered SaaS products.
